brief_summary: A split rectangle. Left half, labeled ZMK Studio, lists amber checkmarks for assigning behaviors to keys, renaming/enabling layers, and selecting physical layouts. Right half, labeled devicetree required, lists warm-red x-marks for combos, conditional layers, behavior properties, and new physical layouts. Visualizes the article's Studio-versus-devicetree boundary.
data_sources: zmk-wireless-split-firmware-guide.mdx § 'ZMK Studio versus hand-written devicetree' — 'Studio is a desktop and web application that lets a builder reassign keys, rename layers, and enable additional layers without reflashing firmware ... assigning behaviors to keys, renaming layers, and switching physical layouts all work today; configuring combos, conditional layers, and behavior properties in the GUI is listed as planned rather than shipped, and defining an entirely new behavior or physical layout isn't a Studio feature at all'
